```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
  out.width = "100%", dpi = 110,
  eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

This vignette runs the standard **surviver** analysis on simulated data
where the true vaccine effectiveness (VE) is known: the epidemic dynamics,
data preparation, model fit, and estimated VE(t) against the truth.

```{r setup}
library(surviver)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
scenarios <- list(Waning = ve_sim_waning, `No waning` = ve_sim_no_waning)
```

## The simulated data

`ve_sim_waning` and `ve_sim_no_waning` were simulated with
[HERMES](https://github.com/lwillem/ibm_hermes), an individual-based model
of transmission through households, schools, workplaces and the community,
developed by Lander Willem (see the
[user manual](https://github.com/lwillem/ibm_hermes/blob/lorentz_center_workshop/doc/user_manual_HERMES.pdf)).
For this package it was extended so that vaccine protection changes with
time since vaccination
([`waning-vaccine-effectiveness` branch](https://github.com/kylieainslie/ibm_hermes/tree/waning-vaccine-effectiveness)).

Each dataset follows 10,000 people for 180 days. Vaccination starts on day 21
and is rolled out in 16 rounds, each vaccinating 3% of those still eligible.
The two scenarios differ only in how protection changes after vaccination:

```{r true-ve, fig.height = 3, fig.alt = "True VE by days since vaccination: both curves rise linearly to 0.8 at day 14; the waning curve then decays towards 0.1, the no-waning curve stays at 0.8."}
true_curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scenarios), function(s) {
  data.frame(scenario = s, t = 0:160, ve = true_ve(0:160, scenarios[[s]]$params))
}))
ggplot(true_curves, aes(t, ve, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Days since vaccination", y = "True VE", colour = NULL)
```

## Epidemic dynamics

`ve_population()` joins the demographic, vaccination and case data into one
row per person. The epidemic peaks while vaccination coverage is still
rising. In the waning scenario, cases among vaccinated people continue to
the end of the study as protection fades.

```{r dynamics, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Daily reported cases split into unvaccinated and vaccinated people, with vaccination coverage overlaid, for each scenario. Cases among vaccinated people grow in the waning scenario as protection fades."}
pops <- lapply(scenarios, ve_population)

daily <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops), function(s) {
  p <- pops[[s]]
  cases <- p[p$infected & p$time_of_reporting <= 180, ]
  vax_at_report <- cases$vaccinated & cases$time_of_vaccination < cases$time_of_reporting
  tab <- as.data.frame(table(day = cases$time_of_reporting,
                             status = ifelse(vax_at_report, "Vaccinated", "Unvaccinated")))
  tab$day <- as.numeric(as.character(tab$day))
  tab$scenario <- s
  tab
}))
coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pops), function(s) {
  v <- pops[[s]]$time_of_vaccination
  data.frame(scenario = s, day = 0:180,
             coverage = sapply(0:180, function(d) mean(!is.na(v) & v <= d)))
}))
scale_k <- max(tapply(daily$Freq, list(daily$day, daily$scenario), sum), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = daily, aes(day, Freq, fill = status), width = 1) +
  geom_step(data = coverage, aes(day, coverage * scale_k), colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)), ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Unvaccinated = "grey65", Vaccinated = "#d95f02")) +
  scale_y_continuous("Reported cases per day",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_k, name = "Vaccination coverage (line)",
                                         labels = scales::percent)) +
  labs(x = "Study day", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Infectious pressure

The model's baseline hazard is driven by the infectious pressure, or force
of infection, each age group experiences on each day. It is built from
reported cases (each assumed infectious for 7 days, starting 2 days before
being reported) and an age-structured contact matrix. `polymod_nl` holds
[POLYMOD](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0050074) contact rates for the Netherlands; `contact_matrix_hermes()` gives
the contact structure HERMES itself uses.

```{r foi, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Infectious pressure by age group over the study for the waning scenario; school-age children face the highest pressure, peaking around days 50 to 80."}
pop <- pops$Waning
inc <- daily_incidence(pop)
prev <- daily_prevalence(inc, duration_infection = 7, reporting_delay = 2)
foi <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop), contact_matrix = polymod_nl)

ggplot(foi, aes(day, Ibar, colour = age_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Study day", y = "Infectious pressure (Ibar)", colour = "Age group",
       title = "Waning scenario")
```

## Preparing the survival data

Each person's follow-up is split at vaccination with `counting_process()`.
People who were infected before vaccination but reported after it would
otherwise be counted as vaccine failures. In practice their infection date is
unknown, so anyone reported within 7 days of vaccination is censored at
vaccination (see the [lab notebook](https://kylieainslie.github.io/surviver/articles/lab-notebook.html),
entry 12). The data are then expanded to person-days and aggregated into
cells for the model.

```{r prepare}
early <- reported_soon_after_vaccination(pop, window = 7)
length(early)

cp <- counting_process(pop, censor_at_vaccination = early)
pd <- expand_person_days(cp)
sd <- make_stan_data(pd, foi)
sd$data[c("N", "K", "T_vax")]
```

Where the information about VE(t) comes from matters. Long times since
vaccination can only be observed late in the study, among people vaccinated
early, so calendar time and time since vaccination are linked. Each
diagonal line below is one vaccination round followed through time; the
top-left corner (long after vaccination, early in the study) can never be
observed:

```{r persontime, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Heat map of vaccinated person-days by study day and days since vaccination, forming a triangle; cases among vaccinated people are overlaid as points and spread across the triangle."}
vac <- pd[pd$vax_status == 1, ]
grid <- aggregate(list(person_days = rep(1, nrow(vac))),
                  by = list(day = vac$day, days_since_vax = vac$days_since_vax), FUN = sum)
events <- vac[vac$event == 1, ]

ggplot(grid, aes(day, days_since_vax)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = person_days)) +
  geom_point(data = events, colour = "#d95f02", size = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey92", high = "grey30") +
  labs(x = "Study day", y = "Days since vaccination", fill = "Vaccinated\nperson-days",
       title = "Waning scenario: vaccinated person-time and cases (points)")
```

## Fitting the model

The model is a Poisson approximation to a Cox model. The log hazard ratio
for vaccination, \(\gamma(t)\), follows a random walk over days since
vaccination, and VE(t) = 1 − exp(\(\gamma(t)\)):

\[
\log \mu = \log\beta + \log \bar I(t_c, a) + \log(\text{person-days}) + \gamma(t)\,V.
\]

Fitting needs [cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) and CmdStan:

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
fit <- fit_ve(sd, seed = 42)
ve <- extract_ve(fit)
expected <- expected_cases(fit, sd, by = c("day", "vax_status"))
```

So that this vignette can be built without CmdStan, the results below are
loaded from fits run in advance with exactly this analysis for both
scenarios (`data-raw/ve_fits.R`).

```{r load-fits}
fits <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ve_fits.rds", package = "surviver"))
# convergence diagnostics and key parameters of each fit
round(sapply(fits[c("waning", "no_waning")], function(f) unlist(f$diagnostics)), 3)
```

### How well does the model fit the cases?

`expected_cases()` sums the model's expected case counts by day and
vaccination status. Comparing them with the observed counts checks that the
infectious pressure and the vaccine effect together reproduce the epidemic
in both groups.

```{r fit-cases, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Observed daily cases (points) and model-expected cases (line with 90% band) for unvaccinated and vaccinated people in both scenarios; the expected curves follow the observed epidemic."}
expected <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(Waning = "waning", `No waning` = "no_waning"), function(k) {
  e <- fits[[k]]$expected
  e$scenario <- if (k == "waning") "Waning" else "No waning"
  e
}))
expected$status <- ifelse(expected$vax_status == 1, "Vaccinated", "Unvaccinated")

ggplot(expected, aes(day)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = status), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean, colour = status), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed, colour = status), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(status ~ factor(scenario, levels = c("Waning", "No waning")),
             scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Unvaccinated = "grey35", Vaccinated = "#d95f02")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Unvaccinated = "grey35", Vaccinated = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(x = "Study day", y = "Cases per day",
       subtitle = "Points: observed. Line and band: model expectation (mean, 90% interval).") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Estimated VE against the truth

```{r fit-ve, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Estimated VE by days since vaccination with 90% credible band against the true curve, from day 8; the estimate tracks the rise and waning in the waning scenario and the plateau in the no-waning scenario, with widening intervals at long times."}
ve <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("waning", "no_waning"), function(k) {
  v <- fits[[k]]$ve
  v$scenario <- if (k == "waning") "Waning" else "No waning"
  v$truth <- true_ve(v$days_since_vax, scenarios[[v$scenario[1]]]$params)
  v
}))
ve <- ve[ve$days_since_vax > 7, ]   # not estimable in the censoring window

ggplot(ve, aes(days_since_vax)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y = truth), colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(scenario, levels = c("Waning", "No waning"))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.6, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Days since vaccination", y = "Vaccine effectiveness",
       subtitle = "Blue: posterior median and 90% interval. Red dashed: true VE.")
```

The model recovers the rise and decline of protection in the waning scenario
and the plateau in the no-waning scenario. Known limitations, all recorded
in the [lab notebook](https://kylieainslie.github.io/surviver/articles/lab-notebook.html):

- time since vaccination is measured to the report date, so the estimate
  lags the true curve by several days, and VE in the first week is not
  estimable after censoring;
- beyond about 90 days the waning scenario's estimate falls below the
  truth, partly because calendar time and time since vaccination are
  linked (see the person-time plot above);
- intervals widen at long times since vaccination, where there are few
  cases.
